title: Sixteen thousand different float keys beyond the range of a double in one flow mapping are sixteen thousand keys or a limit error, in bounded time
notes: The keys are `1e400`, `2e400` ... `16000e400`: sixteen thousand different values, each beyond the range of a double. By the kit's rule for such keys (docs/edit-semantics.md, Refusals) they are all different; a library may instead refuse the document with a `limit` error; it must not call any pair duplicates. The case bounds the cost of telling that: a key identity that compares each new key with every earlier one by exact value is quadratic (about 128 million comparisons here) and a library that rereads the keys on each edit is worse. The edit replaces the value of the last key, found by its text (RFC 6901 section 4), and changes nothing else. The tag `convention` marks the exact-value rule.

provenance.reference: A key lookup for float keys beyond the range of a double that compared a key with all the others, so a flow mapping of sixteen thousand of them took tens of seconds.
